property_summary: After owner calls withdrawAll sending some ETH into C first, the recipient address passed to withdrawAll receives all contract balance (i.e., address(_recipient) gets balance), not the caller.
If the caller is the contract owner then withdrawAll(...) never reverts (i.e., succeeds) for any _recipient.
When withdrawAll is called by the owner, the call never reverts (succeeds) for any provided _recipient and regardless of contract balance.
If withdrawAll is called by an address that is not the owner, the call must revert; otherwise (caller is owner) it must not revert.
If the caller is the owner then withdrawAll(...) never reverts (succeeds); if the caller is not the owner it reverts.

For any caller who is owner and any recipient address, after calling withdrawAll(recipient) the contract's entire balance is sent to the provided recipient (i.e., address(c).balance == 0 and recipient's balance increases) — the mutant that always pays msg.sender can send funds to the caller instead of the specified recipient, violating this property for calls where owner != recipient.
After owner calls withdrawAll, the contract's balance must become zero (all funds are forwarded to the recipient).
If caller is not the owner, withdrawAll must revert (reverted == true); only the owner can successfully call withdrawAll.
If the caller is not the contract's owner, then calling withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).
If caller is not the contract's owner, then calling withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).
If caller is not the contract's owner, then calling withdrawAll must revert (i.e., (caller != owner) == reverted).

For any caller who is the owner and any initial contract balance, calling withdrawAll(recipient) results in the contract's balance becoming zero (all funds forwarded to the recipient); the mutant that calls transfer(0) violates this because the balance remains non-zero for some inputs.
Calling withdrawAll from the contract owner never transfers out the contract balance (owner cannot withdraw to any recipient).

property_summary: Calling withdrawAll as the contract owner always reverts (i.e., cannot be successfully executed by the owner).
Only the owner (c.owner()) can successfully call withdrawAll — calls from non-owners must revert.
After withdrawAll by owner, the contract C remains deployed (its balance may be zero) — i.e., address(c).balance == 0 implies address(c).code.length > 0.
A call to withdrawAll by the owner that does not revert must not cause this contract (the callee) to be destroyed — i.e., if owner calls and call succeeds, then address(c).code.length > 0.
If calling c.withdrawAll(recipient) does not revert, then contract c must still be deployed (address(c).code.length > 0).
If the call to c.withdrawAll(recipient) does not revert, then contract c should still be deployed (address(c).code.length > 0).
If calling c.withdrawAll(recipient) does not revert, then contract c should still be deployed (address(c).code.length > 0).

After any successful withdrawAll(recipient) call by the owner, the contract C remains deployed and its address retains code/balance (i.e., address(c).balance == 0 but contract still exists); the mutant that self-destructs destroys the contract so this property can be violated.

For any recipient and amount sent into C, after the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the contract remains deployed (its code size > 0); the mutant that selfdestructs causes the contract to be destroyed for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any recipient address and any initial balance funded into C by any sender, calling withdrawAll(recipient) by the owner always leaves address(c).balance == 0 and the contract still callable (i.e. subsequent calls to withdrawAll revert for non-owner but do not revert due to missing code) — the mutant that selfdestructs makes the contract address have no code afterwards, breaking the property that the contract's owner getter still returns the owner (i.e., the public owner getter remains callable and returns the original owner after withdrawAll).

For every recipient address and any initial balance, after the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) the public owner getter still returns the original owner (i.e., owner() == deployer); the mutant that selfdestructs may destroy contract and make calls to owner() revert or return nothing, violating this rule for some recipients.

For any recipient address, if the owner calls withdrawAll(recipient) then immediately after the call the contract still exists and its owner() getter remains callable and returns the original owner; the mutant that self-destructs will for some recipient cause the contract to be destroyed so owner() is no longer callable (or returns nothing), breaking this rule.
